status: Unpublished release candidate. Not on npm, under this or any other name. Install from the versioned archive at https://zodiacs.org/examples/, whose SHA-256 is published beside it.

bundled.note: Engine 0.1.1-rc.16 and the site comparison are inlined into server.mjs. The engine was published to npm on 2026-10-01 under the next tag; the bundle is built from the archive whose SHA-256 is below, which npm's tarball matches. Bundling keeps one copy of the comparison rules.

comparison.note: The same module the browser tool at https://zodiacs.org/developers/compare/ runs.

computeApi.note: The hosted compute API's parsers and positions, events and sky-fact calculations, inlined into server.mjs, so get_positions, find_events and check_sky_fact return what POST https://zodiacs.org/api/v1/positions, /events and /sky-fact return for the same request, without a zone.

protocol.note: Revisions observed to negotiate against this server on the wire, one probe each. The official SDK client offers 2025-11-25.

schemas.note: Zodiacs-owned vocabulary, not an industry interoperability standard. The record and receipt schemas are drafts.

changedSince: rc.1 to rc.10, rc.14, rc.15, rc.16, rc.16.1 and rc.16.2 remain unchanged as separate archives; there were no rc.11 to rc.13 archives. The engine is the same 0.1.1-rc.16. New in rc.16.3: nothing a tool does. The compute API gained POST /api/v1/elections, and the modules of src/lib/compute-api/ that this adapter inlines hold the compute API's list of endpoints, its limits, its validation sentences, its receipt and the allowance its searches share, which changed with it, so the bundle changed. get_capabilities lists under sky.limits the same four limits as before, the ones its three sky tools use: it had copied the compute API's whole table of limits, which now also holds the elections endpoint's, and this adapter has no tool for it. Apart from the adapter's version, which the server, get_capabilities, this adapter's own receipts and so the cite.receipt over them, and the methodology resource name, every tool's arguments, results and receipts are rc.16.2's. The README's example comparison now prints the digest of the receipt it shows; rc.16.2's printed rc.16.1's. The adapter itself is still not on npm.
